title: Hazardous Substances & COSHH
whatItIs: The COSHH Regulations 2002 cover substances that can harm health, such as cement, solvents, paints and dusts. They get in by breathing, skin contact, swallowing or the eyes.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST NOT start work that may expose employees to a hazardous substance without a suitable risk assessment.
Exposure MUST be prevented or, where that's not reasonably practicable, adequately controlled.
Where reasonably practicable, a safer substance or process MUST be used instead, e.g. water-based paint.
Other controls MUST come first. PPE is added only where they can't give adequate control.
Employees MUST use the control measures provided and report any defect straight away.

keyFacts: Read the label and the safety data sheet: they tell you the dangers and how to handle the product.

visual.caption: Controlling a hazardous substance, in order of priority

items.title: Eliminate or substitute
items.text: Use a safer substance, form or method, e.g. paste not powder.

items.title: Enclose or extract
items.text: Stop it escaping; extract dust or fumes at the source.

items.title: Fewer people
items.text: Keep anyone not doing the job out of the area.

items.title: PPE last
items.text: Gloves, coveralls, respirator. It must fit the wearer.

a.label: Safety data sheet
points: Written by the supplier of the product
Says what the dangers are and how to store and handle it

b.label: COSHH assessment
points: Made by the employer for the actual job
Decides how exposure will be controlled

onTheTest.question: Under COSHH, when should PPE such as gloves or a respirator be used?
options: Only when the supervisor is on site
When exposure can't be adequately controlled by other means
Instead of ventilation, to save money
onTheTest.why: COSHH reg 7(3): process and engineering controls come first. PPE is added where adequate control can't be achieved by other means.

onTheTest.question: Where should you look first for a new product's hazards and safe handling?
options: The label and the safety data sheet
onTheTest.why: HSG150: suppliers have a legal duty to provide information. Read the label and the safety data sheet.

traps: 'We've always done it this way' isn't a control: some diseases take years to show.
Natural doesn't mean harmless: wood dust can cause asthma.
A dust mask may not stop vapours: the respirator must suit the substance.
